items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: Terry Martin, John Litweiler and J.B. Fighy, the guys who were writing the liner notes for the Delmark records

ctx.x: Well I kind of have to give my dad a lot of appreciation for encouraging that. At one point a conversation I remember well, he and I were driving and he said have you thought about what you want to do when you grow up? I was maybe twelve or thirteen. And I said I don’t know. And he said well when I was your age I wanted to be a writer. And again I thought that’s okay? That would be okay? So he said to me at the time, the people who you’re reading though, most of them were reporters first, and many of them were…

I was putting out. I was on the high school newspaper. And when we moved to the suburbs that was pretty good actually journalistic training. It was a weekly paper and it was substantial for a high school paper. And when I was in college also I was the counterculture editor of the college paper for a while, in Syracuse University. And of course there was a big explosion of music in the late sixties, and I did connect with pop music at that time, Jimi Hendrix, Aretha Franklin, Motown and some rock & roll,…
Basically getting to know the whole scene as much as you can. I mean you said an important thing there, to write only what you know or feel strongly about.
